newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PBL sees higher tv, magazines EBIT.
newsitem.headline: PBL sees higher tv, magazines EBIT.

text.p: Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd said on Wednesday it expected both its television and magazine divisions to post an increase in earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) in the current year.
However, it said the strength of the advertising market was difficult to assess, making it impossible to predict the quantum of the increase.
"We expect both television and magazines to post an increase in EBIT this year," PBL managing director James Packer said.
"Our goal continues to be to provide our viewers and readers with the best possible products while maintaining a tight control on costs," Packer said in a statement.
"Our franchises in both television and magazines, while facing unprecedented levels of new competition are as strong as they have ever been," he said.
Packer said advertising markets for both television and magazines weakened in the second half of the year.
EBIT for television rose 14.9 percent for the year.
PBL's top rating Nine Network increased its share of the advertising market in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane to 41.9 percent from 41.4 percent, Packer said.

"While television had another excellent year, Magazines' financial performance suffered as a result of the dramatic increase in paper prices and a generally lacklustre trading environment," Packer said.
Magazines' EBIT was down 11.3 percent in the second half and 6.4 percent lower in the year.

Magazine revenue from international operations rose 13.4 percent in the year, but profits were lower due to a poor result from Australian Consolidated Press' U.K. operations and higher expenditure related to the launch of Cleo Malaysia and Cleo New Zealand.
During the year, PBL sold its half interest in Sky Channel for a A$19.5 million gain and its minority interest in Village Roadshow Ltd for a A$84.4 million gain.

"The gain for these sales was partially offset by provisions totalling A$51.2 million against investments generally, doubtful loans relating to sporting rights and the abandonment of a television barter activity in China, resulting in a net abnormal gain of A$52.7 million," Packer said.
He said PBL increased its holding in newspaper publisher John Fairfax Holdings Ltd to 14.9 percent.
At a share price of A$2.61, PBL's Fairfax investment is worth A$11.7 million more than its costs.
"Our goal continues to be to increase our involvement in Fairfax subject to market conditions and regulatory constraints," Packer said.
He said also that PBL's involvement in a funding package for troubled pay television operator Australis Media Ltd would see PBL convert short-term funding into a long-term equity position.
"We believe that Australis can, if refinanced, build a valuable business based on its satellite and microwave operations and its position as a programme provider to Foxtel," Packer said.
